Description: the patient has reported clinicallly significant manic or hypomanic symptoms

Just last week, I stayed up all night organizing a huge party for my friends, getting everything ready and even planning out games and activities. The next morning, I realized I hadn't slept and felt invincible, talking a mile a minute, but now I worry if I overdid it. It's strange because one minute I feel on top of the world, and the next, I crash back into that low place.

Generally, I feel pretty low and unmotivated, and those high-energy moments are rare and usually followed by a long period of feeling down. Although I had that one intense night organizing the party, it was just a brief spike in energy, and I quickly fell back into my usual low state. I typically struggle to maintain any kind of consistent mood and mostly feel drained and unmotivated, so I don't think I've met that threshold.

Last month, I spent three straight weekends throwing together surprise outings for my friends, feeling like I could conquer anything. But then, those high times always crash into these deep lows where it feels like even getting out of bed is a monumental task, and I end up spending days in a funk, struggling to motivate myself. It's a tough pattern that seems to repeat itself, and I can't help but wonder if it's something more.

Other specified bipolar and related disorders or unspecified bipolar and related disorders

The criteria are met if the patient has experienced one or more major depressive episodes without any history of manic or hypomanic episodes. To determine if a major depressive episode has occurred, the following aspects must be examined:
1. Interest or pleasure in doing things
2. Sleeping conditions
3. Energy level
4. Appetite
5. Feelings of self-worth
6. Concentration when doing things
7. Changes in movement or speech
8. Suicidal ideation
9. Duration of at least 2 weeks
The decision should be based on an overall assessment of the severity of these aspects, considering the patient's responses across all areas (not all aspects need to be abnormal). The duration of symptoms should be explicitly asked and confirmed as lasting at least 2 weeks before making a final decision. Be really caucious when making the decision!
Patient_Story: Over the past couple of weeks, I've found myself really struggling with getting out of bed most mornings; it feels like the weight of the world is pressing down on me. I used to love cooking for my family, but lately, even just making a simple meal feels exhausting, and my appetite has shrunk significantly—I hardly eat anything now. I know I’m upset about my grandmother’s passing, but I can still manage to get through my workday without feeling completely lost or useless, so I wonder if this might just be a sad phase rather than something more serious.

Description: persistent depressive disorder

While I have tough days, I’m still able to go to work and interact with friends, so it doesn't disrupt my life in a cyclical way.
